# Story 26 — FAQs & Help Articles

> Note: this is the first plan under `.squad/plans/knowledge-base/`. The story number **26** is chosen to align with the intake, which explicitly references sibling stories **Story 27 — Solutions & Guides** and **Story 28 — Knowledge Base Search**. Follow-up plans for the same feature slug should continue from 27, 28.

## Prerequisites

- Existing authentication and role/permission model (roles: `Administrator`, `Manager`, `Agent`, `Customer`) — see `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Roles/` and `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Authorization/`.
- Existing permission-based authorization pipeline (`HasPermissionAttribute`, `PermissionPolicyProvider`, `PermissionAuthorizationHandler`) already in use across controllers such as `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/Tickets/Tickets/TicketsController.cs`.
- Existing DB seeding pattern for new permissions in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Infrastructure/Persistence/DbSeeder.cs` and permission constants in `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Domain/Roles/Permissions.cs`.
- **Story 28 (Knowledge Base Search)** will consume the tables and read APIs delivered by this story. Coordinate with that story's owner on the query shape (published-only, visibility-filtered).
- **Story 27 (Solutions & Guides)** — related but scoped separately; keep the `KnowledgeBase*` model isolated from Solutions/Guides so both can evolve.

---

## Story Goal

Deliver Knowledge Base content management for **FAQs** and **Help Articles**, sharing a common entity type with a discriminator, and exposing role-appropriate read and write APIs plus UI. Explicit outcomes:

1. Administrators and Managers can create, edit, and publish FAQ and Help Article items via API and UI.
2. Every item stores **question/title**, **body (answer/content)**, **category**, **content type** (`Faq` / `HelpArticle`), **audience** (`CustomerFacing` / `Internal`), and **publication status** (`Draft` / `Published`).
3. Agents get read-only access to all **published** items (both audiences).
4. Customers get read-only access to **published** items where audience is **CustomerFacing**.
5. Server-side authorization enforces the matrix above; UI reflects it but is not the only check.
6. Categories are stored per-item as a lightweight `KnowledgeBaseCategory` table so search (Story 28) can filter by category.

**Not in scope:** search / ranking, notifications, versioning, workflows beyond direct publish, ticket-to-article conversion, Solutions & Guides.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Draft** is the default status on create. Published visibility must never bypass the `Published` filter for Agent/Customer readers.
- **Audience is authoritative for Customer visibility**: `Internal` items must never be returned to a Customer principal, even when published.
- **Content type** distinguishes `Faq` (question/answer) from `HelpArticle` (title/content). Both share the same table but validation differs (see body validation below).
- Only `Administrator` and `Manager` may write or publish. Agents and Customers are strictly read-only.
- Category is a foreign key to `KnowledgeBaseCategory`; do **not** reuse `TicketCategory`.

```csharp
namespace CustomerSupportCrm.Domain.KnowledgeBase;

public enum KnowledgeBaseContentType
{
    Faq = 1,
    HelpArticle = 2,
}

public enum KnowledgeBaseAudience
{
    CustomerFacing = 1,
    Internal = 2,
}

public enum KnowledgeBasePublicationStatus
{
    Draft = 1,
    Published = 2,
}

public class KnowledgeBaseArticle
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public KnowledgeBaseContentType ContentType { get; set; }
    public KnowledgeBaseAudience Audience { get; set; }
    public KnowledgeBasePublicationStatus Status { get; set; } = KnowledgeBasePublicationStatus.Draft;

    // For Faq this is the Question; for HelpArticle this is the Title.
    public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    // For Faq this is the Answer; for HelpArticle this is the Content (long-form).
    public string Body { get; set; } = string.Empty;

    public Guid CategoryId { get; set; }
    public KnowledgeBaseCategory? Category { get; set; }

    public Guid CreatedByUserId { get; set; }
    public DateTime CreatedAtUtc { get; set; }
    public Guid? UpdatedByUserId { get; set; }
    public DateTime? UpdatedAtUtc { get; set; }
    public Guid? PublishedByUserId { get; set; }
    public DateTime? PublishedAtUtc { get; set; }
}
```

### 7 — Service interface + implementation

Create files:

- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/KnowledgeBase/IKnowledgeBaseArticlesService.cs`
- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/KnowledgeBase/KnowledgeBaseArticlesService.cs`
- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/KnowledgeBase/IKnowledgeBaseCategoriesService.cs`
- `backend/src/CustomerSupportCrm.Api/KnowledgeBase/KnowledgeBaseCategoriesService.cs`

Service methods for **articles**:

- `Task<IReadOnlyList<KnowledgeBaseArticleDto>> ListAsync(KnowledgeBaseListQuery query, ClaimsPrincipal user, CancellationToken ct)` — filters:
  - `contentType?` (Faq/HelpArticle)
  - `status?` (Draft/Published) — **ignored** and forced to `Published` for Agent/Customer callers.
  - `audience?` — for Customer callers, forced to `CustomerFacing`.
  - `categoryId?`
- `Task<KnowledgeBaseArticleDto?> GetAsync(Guid id, ClaimsPrincipal user, CancellationToken ct)` — applies the same visibility rules; returns null (→ 404) if not visible.
- `Task<KnowledgeBaseArticleDto> CreateAsync(CreateKnowledgeBaseArticleRequest req, Guid userId, CancellationToken ct)` — always starts `Draft`; validates title/body non-empty and category exists.
- `Task<KnowledgeBaseArticleDto> UpdateAsync(Guid id, UpdateKnowledgeBaseArticleRequest req, Guid userId, CancellationToken ct)` — allowed regardless of status; updates `UpdatedByUserId` / `UpdatedAtUtc`.
- `Task<KnowledgeBaseArticleDto> PublishAsync(Guid id, Guid userId, CancellationToken ct)` — sets `Status=Published`, stamps `PublishedAtUtc`. Idempotent when already published.
- `Task<KnowledgeBaseArticleDto> UnpublishAsync(Guid id, Guid userId, CancellationToken ct)` — sets `Status=Draft`; clears `PublishedAtUtc`.
- `Task DeleteAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken ct)` — hard delete allowed for Admin/Manager (out-of-scope of AC but useful for cleanup; keep as separate permission gate on `KnowledgeBaseArticlesManage`).

**Visibility rule** encapsulated in a private helper `bool CanSeeInternal(ClaimsPrincipal user)` that returns true when the user has `KnowledgeBaseArticlesViewInternal`.

Categories service: `List`, `Create`, `Update`, `Delete` mirroring `TicketCategoriesService`. Prevent delete when any article references it (return 409-style domain error, matches ticket categories pattern).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Customer requests an internal article by id** — service must return 404 (not 403) to avoid leaking existence. Enforced in `KnowledgeBaseArticlesService.GetAsync` after applying the audience/status filter.
- **Agent requests a Draft** — same as above: 404, not 403.
- **Publishing an already-published item** — idempotent; service returns the DTO unchanged. No history event required by this story.
- **Category delete while articles reference it** — return `409 Conflict` with a domain message; do not cascade. Mirrors ticket categories behaviour.
- **Empty title or body** — service returns `400` with a validation error. Trim before validating.
- **Very long body (Help Article)** — no maximum enforced at DB level (nvarchar(max)); UI textarea is unbounded but limit paste to a sane 200 KB client-side hint.
- **ContentType mutation on update** — API must reject changing `ContentType`; `UpdateKnowledgeBaseArticleRequest` intentionally omits it, and the service ignores any attempt.
- **Concurrent publish** — last write wins; both requests succeed; no versioning in this story (out of scope).
- **Unicode in question/title** — must round-trip; ensure DB columns are `nvarchar` (default with EF Core SQL Server).
- **Customer with no assigned KB permission** — cannot hit list/detail; expect `403`. Seeder must assign `KnowledgeBaseArticlesView` to Customer role.
- **Category name uniqueness** — DB unique index; service maps `DbUpdateException` → `400` with "Category already exists".

## Migration / Rollback

- Migration adds two independent tables and their indexes. No changes to existing tables.
- Rollback: `dotnet ef migrations remove` (before deploy) or apply the down migration (drops both tables). Because no existing data references KB tables, rollback is safe.
- Seeder is idempotent (guard each permission and each starter category by key/name before insert) so re-running does not duplicate rows.
